translation_notes: initNs={'odml': ..., 'rdf': RDF, 'rdfs': RDFS} becomes three @prefix declarations, none of them interpolated in the query body: the site is pure prefix binding, no initBindings term. This is the 'prologue herite des @prefix' half of the bind_initbindings row, not the term-interpolation half.

ODML_NS is a plain string built at run time in the source repo (imported from odml.tools.rdf_converter), so the odml: prefix uses a formatted IRI (f<{ODML_NS}>) rather than a literal <...> -- declarations.md documents this exact case (a computed prefix IRI).

The region only prepares the query (prepareQuery / s{ }); it is never iterated where it is written. The driver therefore runs q against a fixture graph via the call suffix (q(g) for the ldpy PreparedQuery, graph.query(q) for rdflib) to compare something observable -- constructing a query has no other externally visible effect.

RECLASSIFIED (repair 2026-10-27) directly-expressible -> minor-restructuring. The repository uses `q` on the very next line as `for row in graph.query(q): print(row.d, row.s)`. The value of s{ } is an ldpy PreparedQuery, not an rdflib Query: `graph.query(q)` raises `AttributeError: 'PreparedQuery' object has no attribute 'algebra'` (the old driver hid this by calling g.query(q) on one side and q(g) on the other). The language cannot reproduce the repository's interface: every consumer must be rewritten to `for row in q(graph)` (same ResultRow, row.d/row.s unchanged). Keeping `prepareQuery(...)` would be plain rdflib, not a construction. The driver now exercises the repository's real consumer on both sides (rdflib: graph.query(q); ldpy: q(g)), compares (row.d, row.s) and the projected variables, and asserts the interface gap as a probe (verdict key interface_gap). Also: the site uses initNs only (-> @prefix), no initBindings, so it does not exercise the term-interpolation half of the bind_initbindings stratum. Fixture extended with three neighbours that must not match (non-Document parent, child not typed Section, case-different hasType).
